sources.title: Julia Farley, British Museum: Who were the Celts?
sources.note: Curator account, 2015: connected but distinct communities, Britain/Ireland not explicitly called Celtic by classical authors, Roman conquest and later changing identities.

sources.title: Hampshire County Council: Danebury Iron Age hillfort
sources.note: Site custodian, Life at Danebury section; roundhouses, grain storage, livestock, crafts, imported resources and suggested exports.

sources.title: South West Heritage Trust: Iron Age roundhouse at Avalon Archaeology
sources.note: Current reconstruction explicitly based on excavated Glastonbury Lake Village evidence. Do not describe the modern reconstruction as an ancient surviving house. Page gives inconsistent 100/150-year settlement duration; neither used.

sources.title: English Heritage: History of Maiden Castle
sources.note: Everyday life in the Iron Age, fields, managed woodland and animal uses. No unsupported generalisation of castle battle cemetery into all inhabitants.

sources.title: National Museum of Ireland: Archaeology museum guide
sources.note: Printed pp. 14 to 15 and 20 to 23, Doogarrymore fourth-century-BCE wheels, third-century-BCE Ardnaglug collars and Broighter hoard. Full PDF inspected.

sources.title: National Museum of Ireland: Bog Bodies Research Project
sources.note: Museum research account; two bodies around 400 to 200 BCE, discovery 2003, multidisciplinary imaging and dietary research.

sources.title: Melanie Giles: Strands of Evidence in Later Prehistory
sources.note: 2016 scholarly afterword, section Hair; Clonycavan hair with imported resin. Proposed ritual explanations not presented as certainty.

sources.title: British Museum: Money Gallery large-print guide, British inscribed coins
sources.note: Case 2, Britain’s first inscribed coins, item 3: COMMIOS, southern England c. 40 to 25 BCE. Indexed original exact inscription inspected; direct PDF fetch errored. Existing carthaginian-empire uses this URL; combined budget explicitly checked.

sources.title: Spanish Ministry of Culture: Bracara historical place authority
sources.note: Official historical thesaurus; indexed original checked for Braga capital, councils 561/572 and conquest 585. The page’s overgeneralised fifth-century conversion statement is not used.

sources.title: Municipality of Braga: the Dume museum and archaeological remains
sources.note: 18 May 2018 municipal account, cathedral/basilica and monastery beneath present church; Roman bath complex distinguished from Suevic structures.

sources.title: José Carlos Sánchez Pardo: economic foundations in Suevic-Visigothic Gallaecia
sources.note: Anuario de Estudios Medievales 44/2 (2014), pp. 983 to 1020; printed p. 986, Vigo long-distance imports in fourth to seventh centuries. Indexed original full passage inspected; direct PDF access errored. Narrow summary only, not unsupported specific cargo claims.

sources.title: Late pottery at the Castro of Viladonga, fourth to sixth centuries
sources.note: Croa 28, full original PDF, printed pp. 43, 47 to 49. Authors date intensive occupation fifth/early-sixth centuries and propose abandonment in first half sixth; not every object precisely dated to 500s or ethnically Suevic.

sources.title: Xunta de Galicia: official descriptions of protected historical coins
sources.note: Official inventory annex 3.1 to 3.2, Suevic tremisses in Honorius and Valentinian names, 1.35g each. Promotional earliest-state claims and disputed peace legend interpretation omitted.

sources.title: Martin of Braga: De correctione rusticorum
sources.note: Primary Latin work in modern online transcription, sections 15 to 17. Author’s prescriptions/condemnations are attributed as such, not universal population behaviour.

sources.title: Consello da Cultura Galega: Como levar unha vida honesta
sources.note: Official 2023 scholarly-edition record, Miro commission, classical ethics, extensive later Latin transmission. Direct indexed catalogue checked.

sources.title: Martin of Braga: Formula vitae honestae
sources.note: Primary Latin in modern transcription, section 2. Exact phrase De dubiis non definias; English rendering supplied here, not a medieval translation.

sources.title: Museo Arqueolóxico de Ourense: the inscription from San Pedro de Rocas
sources.note: Francisco Javier Pérez Rodríguez, February 2017. Exact transcription and critical discussion of a probable ninth/tenth-century copy of the text dated 573; uncertain names and donation/foundation meaning.

proposedOverrides.summary: The later Suevic kingdom of northwestern Iberia, its trade, Christian institutions and sixth-century writers.

batchIdentityNotes.note: Snapshots mostly Britain/Ireland; 200 BCE snapshot has anomalous southwest continental extension to 41.44N. Public overview flags that extension and rejects a single polity/ethnic boundary. Does not duplicate Continental La Tène, Boii or Celtiberian polity narratives. No later ogham projected into BCE coverage. Writing COMMIOS directly from BM label, dated 40 to 25 BCE.

Decoded single 500 to 600 snapshot is NW Iberia, not continental Suebi/Suebian-knot populations. Map coverage extends 15 years after conquest; public overview, periods and ending say so. No 409/411 foedus certainty or universal conversion date. Viladonga evidence explicitly spans fifth/early-sixth centuries; Roman Dume baths not asserted functioning under Suevic kings. Writing Latin, not invented Germanic speech; Rocas later-copy issue explicit.
